newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa told to expect media criticism.
newsitem.headline: South Africa told to expect media criticism.

text.p: South Africa should not expect all reports on it by the foreign media to be positive and glowing, Commonwealth Press Union (CPU) president Sir David English said on Monday.

Opening the CPU's biennial conference in Cape Town, English said that since the 1994 elections, the foreign press had tended to look at South Africa through rose-coloured glasses but it was just another country.
"It is not paradise. It is a young multi-cultural state, there is much potential here and we will see that and report it.
"But we may also see things that you may not want us to see, things which perhaps even you chose not to see yourselves. But newspapers must see everything...that's our job," English said.

"Not every report will be glowing. We will write about your achievements, your energy and your dynamism but we shall focus on your problems too, on crime, housing, education, the economy and the curse of corruption.
"Such problems are present in all countries today and South Africa is no exception and it is the press's duty to spotlight both the good and the bad. Democracy really demands it."
He said the fact that South Africa was hosting the conference indicated that South Africa was no longer afraid of a free press.
English, who is chairman and editor in chief of Britain's Associated Newspapers Ltd, said that apartheid governments went to considerable lengths to control foreign press reporting.
"The outside world as a whole did not get a true perspective of South Africa and that is why so many publications had such gloomy forecasts about this nation.
"The accepted view was that disaster and not democracy was the only future for this country. The people of this country proved us wrong."
English said the press not inherently hostile to the new South African government.

President Nelson Mandela and other leaders of the ruling African National Congress have frequently upbraided the media for being too critical of their government, saying some reports have been racist.
